page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top left. Catchword "per" at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.p: stemus substantiam præcepti: Apostoli nihil immutarūt. Manet enim adhuc dies unus in septimana, quo feriantur omnes ab operibus & negotiis huius sæculi, & vacatur cultui divino. Sed si spectes accidens: damus, illud esse mutatum. Sed hoc non pugnat cum voluntate Dei in præcepto de sabbatho. Nam quicquid fuit ceremoniale, illud post Christum, liberum mansit Ecclesiæ, idque ex voluntate Dei.

Neque vero sine causa, diem sabbathi, quod ad suum attinet accidens, mutarunt in alium diem. Nam utile erat Ecclesiæ, ut hac libertate uterentur Apostoli, quò universis patefieret, Messiam advenisse, eoq; ceremo-niis omnibus finem esse impositum.

Lex enim usque ad Christum: & illa ceremonia usque ad tempus correctionis imposita, Hebr. 9. 10. Hac de causa etiam Paulus Coloss. 2. monet fideles, ut hanc dierum libertatem retineant, nec sinant se in servitutem Mosaicæ legis de sabbathis redigi, cum ait, Nemo vos iudicet in cibo & potu, aut de parte diei festi, aut sabbathorum. Ergo propter hanc libertatem Christianis asserendam, utile fuit mutare sabbathum. Quòd vero non in alium, sed in diem proximè insequentem sabbathum, qui Solis apud Gentes, & fit primus Iudæis, & Dominicus Christianis dicitur, mutarint, duplicem adfert Iustinus in Apologia ad Antoninum, causam: primam, quòd eo die Deus creauit Mundum

page.notes: Page number "198" read from a small mark at the top left, somewhat faded. The first word is a worn initial read as "s" (probably "stemus", the continuation of "statuemus" from the previous page); the first paragraph is therefore a fragment. "imposita" in the Lex paragraph carries a doubtful final letter; it is printed as "imposita" with a slightly different letter form and should be checked against the scan. The Latin word "diuino" is a printed spelling kept as "divino" under the u/v rule. "Hebr. 9. 10." and "Coloss. 2." are inline references, not marginal notes.
